title: Build a Web Page: HTML and CSS
subject: computing

sections.body:
HTML gives a page its STRUCTURE using tags:

for a big heading,

for a paragraph, for a link, for an image.
CSS controls STYLE: colours, fonts, spacing. Example: h1 { color: green; }
Browsers read HTML and CSS and display the page. Anyone can view a page's code with 'View source'.

Make a page about your hobby with a heading, a paragraph and a list (
  • …
).

quiz.q: Which HTML tag makes a paragraph?
hints: The tag's letter is the first letter of 'paragraph'.
is for headings and for images. Which is left for paragraphs?
If HTML is a house's walls and rooms, CSS is the paint and decoration.
quiz.explain: CSS controls the style: colours, fonts, layout and spacing.

quiz.q: What does the CSS rule h1 { color: green; } do?
options: Makes the text of big headings green
Makes the text of every paragraph green
Adds a new green heading to the page's structure
hints: The part before the curly brackets says WHICH elements the rule applies to.
Inside the brackets is the property being styled and its new value. Does CSS add content, or style what is already there?
p { font-size: 20px; } makes the text inside paragraphs 20 pixels tall. It doesn't add any new paragraphs.
quiz.explain: h1 picks out the big headings, and color: green sets their text colour. CSS changes style; it doesn't add structure (that's HTML's job).
